newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 28.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Thursday:
- AT&T Corp said it would raise long-distance phone rates by 5.9 percent, the largest rate hike in nearly three years.
- U.S. officials have expanded its inquiry into alcohol advertisements and are examining whether Stroh Brewing Co is running television advertisements that are aimed at underaged viewers.

- A long, bitter dispute between twins who jointly own a majority of Value Line Inc has been settled. The settlement requires that the family holding company buyout one twin's stake in the holding company for an undisclosed sum by early January.

- Other nations may be following the United States' curb on corruptions and bribes. International development funds, economic alliances and the International Chamber of Commerce have all taken steps to curb corruption.
- The Dow Jones industrial average slid 29.07 points to 6,499.34 on Wednesday as Walt Disney Co and oil shares fell with profit taking before the Thanksgiving holiday.
- The U.S. economy's growth was slower in the third quarter than initially estimated -- two percent compared to 2.2 percent, the Commerce Department said.

- AT&T upset Japanese competitors by offering to provide discount international calls to Japanese customers, using a "call-back" technique to make calls technically originate in America, where rates are lower.
- Cardinal Health Inc said it would buy Owen Healthcare Inc for $27.25 a share or $496 million in stock.
- The Clinton Administration proposed tighter air quality standards, but industry groups criticized the proposals as costly and unnecesary.

- L.A. Gear Inc said it would cut 170 jobs or 55 percent of its workforce and that its president William Benford would leave. It also plans other cost cuts and will take a charge of $28 million to $33 million.
- Canadian Government, union and airline officials are working to keep Canadian Airlines Corp in the air.
- Bre-X Minerals Ltd is in talks ordered by the Indonesian Government to sell 75 percent of its $4.44 billion gold deposit on the island of Borneo to Barrick Gold Corp of Toronto.
